cells.brief: List 50 distinct ideas for reducing food waste in a mid-size city. Number them 1 to 50. One sentence each.
cells.text:
1. Offer households free food-waste audits to identify their biggest sources of waste.
2. Run a public campaign on planning meals before shopping.
3. Distribute reusable shopping lists organized by store section.
4. Teach residents how to interpret “best before” and expiration dates.
5. Offer workshops on storing produce to extend its freshness.
6. Create a citywide directory of places that accept surplus food.
7. Fund neighborhood community fridges with regular safety inspections.
8. Coordinate volunteers to transport surplus meals from businesses to shelters.
9. Give restaurants grants to buy equipment for safely storing surplus food.
10. Connect grocery stores with food banks through a real-time donation platform.
11. Help schools donate unopened surplus meals where regulations permit.
12. Encourage cafeterias to use smaller serving utensils and offer second helpings.
13. Let students preorder school lunches so kitchens can prepare accurate quantities.
14. Train school cafeteria staff to track and reduce kitchen waste.
15. Add share tables in schools for unopened, unwanted food.
16. Offer restaurants tools to forecast demand using past sales data.
17. Encourage restaurants to offer smaller portion options.
18. Provide reusable containers for customers to take leftovers home.
19. Promote discounted end-of-day sales of unsold prepared food.
20. Create a city-backed marketplace for imperfect produce.
21. Help farmers sell surplus crops through pop-up neighborhood markets.
22. Organize volunteer gleaning teams to harvest crops that would otherwise be left in fields.
23. Connect local farmers with processors who can turn surplus produce into shelf-stable products.
24. Support commercial kitchens that make soups and sauces from donated surplus ingredients.
25. Encourage grocery stores to sell individual fruits and vegetables rather than only large packs.
26. Ask retailers to place soon-to-expire items in clearly marked discount sections.
27. Provide small businesses with guidance on safe food donation.
28. Recognize businesses that meet measurable food-waste reduction goals.
29. Include food-waste prevention requirements in city catering contracts.
30. Require large municipal events to develop surplus-food donation plans.
31. Help event organizers estimate attendance and adjust catering orders.
32. Offer cooking classes focused on using leftovers creatively.
33. Publish seasonal recipes that use commonly wasted ingredients.
34. Teach residents how to freeze food safely in convenient portions.
35. Create a neighborhood exchange for homegrown produce.
36. Partner with apartment managers to share food-storage tips with tenants.
37. Work with employers to reduce overordering for meetings and office events.
38. Encourage hotels to replace oversized buffets with smaller batches replenished as needed.
39. Help hospitals tailor meal orders to patients’ preferences and schedules.
40. Support care homes in adjusting menus based on residents’ feedback and plate waste.
41. Introduce pay-as-you-feel community meals made with safe surplus ingredients.
42. Train food pantry staff to manage inventory using a first-in, first-out system.
43. Provide food pantries with refrigeration to accept more perishable donations.
44. Coordinate donation pickup schedules so charities receive food they can distribute promptly.
45. Create a municipal dashboard tracking food waste and recovery over time.
46. Provide grants for businesses to measure food waste by source.
47. Convene retailers, charities, farmers, and residents to coordinate local prevention efforts.
48. Pilot neighborhood drop-off points for surplus shelf-stable food.
49. Provide compost collection for unavoidable food scraps after edible food has been prioritized for people.
50. Arrange for suitable food scraps to become animal feed where local rules allow.

cells.brief: List 50 distinct ideas for reducing food waste in a mid-size city. Number them 1 to 50. One sentence each.
cells.text:
1. Create a citywide app that matches surplus food from businesses with nearby charities in real time.
2. Install refrigerated community lockers where residents can share unopened surplus food.
3. Run a fleet of electric cargo bikes to collect donations from restaurants and shops.
4. Organize volunteer gleaning crews to harvest produce left in nearby fields.
5. Open a pay-what-you-can grocery store stocked with surplus food.
6. Launch a “last-hour” map showing restaurants and bakeries selling discounted leftovers.
7. Help school cafeterias forecast attendance so they prepare more accurate quantities.
8. Place supervised share tables in schools for unopened items students do not want.
9. Offer residents free workshops on meal planning, storage, and using leftovers.
10. Print simple storage tips on city-issued reusable produce bags.
11. Host neighborhood “cook the fridge” nights where residents turn surplus ingredients into shared meals.
12. Create a lending library of dehydrators, pressure canners, and other food-preservation equipment.
13. Train apartment-building volunteers to coordinate safe food sharing among neighbors.
14. Establish a municipal kitchen where donated produce can be turned into soups and sauces.
15. Give restaurants grants to redesign menus around ingredients already in stock.
16. Encourage caterers to offer smaller default portions with free additional servings on request.
17. Introduce a voluntary citywide certification for businesses that measure and reduce food waste.
18. Provide grocery stores with forecasting tools that account for local events and weather.
19. Ask supermarkets to sell cosmetically imperfect produce in prominently displayed bargain sections.
20. Create a subscription box featuring surplus produce from local farms and wholesalers.
21. Arrange for farmers’ market vendors to donate unsold goods before packing up.
22. Set up a hotline for event organizers to arrange rapid pickup of excess prepared food.
23. Require city-funded events to have a surplus-food donation plan.
24. Build cold-storage hubs where small charities can temporarily hold donated perishables.
25. Coordinate recurring food-rescue stops along existing municipal vehicle routes.
26. Offer food-safety training to volunteer drivers and community fridge organizers.
27. Partner with hospitals to adjust patient meal orders closer to serving time.
28. Help hotels replace oversized breakfast buffets with smaller, frequently replenished displays.
29. Encourage restaurants to offer diners smaller portions at proportionately lower prices.
30. Run a public campaign explaining the difference between quality dates and food-safety guidance.
31. Invite local chefs to publish recipes using commonly discarded stems, leaves, and peels.
32. Create a school competition for student-designed food-waste reduction projects.
33. Add food-waste audits to free sustainability consultations for small businesses.
34. Negotiate discounts on inventory-management software for independent grocers.
35. Connect food manufacturers with organizations that can use safe surplus ingredients.
36. Host a regular marketplace where businesses can trade surplus packaging, ingredients, and supplies.
37. Give community gardens access to safe, locally produced compost made from inedible scraps.
38. Collect unavoidable food scraps separately and process them into biogas.
39. Offer households smaller trash bins and convenient food-scrap collection to encourage sorting.
40. Install smart scales in municipal kitchens to reveal which dishes generate the most leftovers.
41. Publish an annual city food-waste dashboard with neighborhood and sector-level trends.
42. Recruit grocery cashiers to explain discounts on soon-to-expire products.
43. Partner with delivery platforms to highlight affordable surplus meals alongside regular listings.
44. Create a rapid-response team to rescue food when refrigeration equipment fails.
45. Coordinate with transit hubs to donate unsold food from station vendors at closing time.
46. Help food pantries accept smaller, more frequent deliveries so produce reaches people sooner.
47. Offer grants for shared commercial freezers that let food businesses store surplus safely.
48. Organize seasonal preserving days for excess fruit from public trees and consenting homeowners.
49. Develop a city procurement policy favoring suppliers with credible food-waste reduction plans.
50. Invite residents to adopt fruit trees in public spaces and coordinate harvests before the fruit falls.

cells.brief: List 50 distinct ideas for reducing food waste in a mid-size city. Number them 1 to 50. One sentence each.
cells.text:
1. Create a citywide food-rescue network connecting businesses with charities that can use their surplus.
2. Offer households free meal-planning workshops at libraries and community centers.
3. Distribute shopping-list templates that help residents buy only what they need.
4. Teach residents how to understand “best before” and “use by” labels.
5. Run a clear, simple campaign showing how to store common foods.
6. Help grocery stores mark down food approaching its expiration date.
7. Encourage retailers to sell misshapen produce at a discount.
8. Set up a shared online marketplace for surplus food from local businesses.
9. Provide small grants for restaurants to measure and reduce kitchen waste.
10. Encourage restaurants to offer smaller portions at lower prices.
11. Make take-home containers readily available at restaurants.
12. Help caterers plan quantities using attendance data from previous events.
13. Establish donation procedures for safe, unserved food from public events.
14. Train school cafeteria staff to adjust production based on what students actually eat.
15. Invite students to help design school menus they are more likely to enjoy.
16. Create supervised school share tables for eligible unopened food.
17. Schedule lunch with enough time for students to eat.
18. Help hospitals tailor meal sizes and menus to patients’ needs.
19. Offer workplace cafeterias tools to forecast daily demand.
20. Encourage hotels to replenish breakfast buffets in smaller batches.
21. Organize volunteer gleaning teams to harvest crops left in nearby fields.
22. Connect farmers with buyers who can use surplus or imperfect produce.
23. Support community kitchens that turn donated surplus produce into meals.
24. Establish refrigerated community fridges with clear food-safety rules.
25. Fund refrigerated vehicles for organizations transporting donated food.
26. Coordinate donation pickups so small businesses can share a collection route.
27. Help food pantries request donations based on what their clients need.
28. Extend food-pantry hours so donated food reaches people sooner.
29. Train food-rescue volunteers in safe handling and temperature control.
30. Offer businesses easy-to-use guidance on local food-donation rules.
31. Create a recognition program for businesses that consistently prevent food waste.
32. Ask city-funded institutions to include waste-reduction targets in food contracts.
33. Conduct regular waste audits in municipal kitchens to identify avoidable losses.
34. Label near-expiry inventory so staff can use it first.
35. Install temperature monitors in public food-storage facilities to catch equipment failures.
36. Offer rebates to small food businesses that upgrade unreliable refrigeration.
37. Teach residents how to freeze bread, leftovers, and seasonal produce.
38. Publish recipes that use commonly discarded ingredients such as vegetable stems.
39. Organize neighborhood cooking classes focused on using leftovers.
40. Encourage residents to designate an “eat first” shelf in their refrigerators.
41. Create a produce-sharing program for gardeners with excess harvests.
42. Help apartment buildings organize safe, monitored food-sharing stations.
43. Partner with delivery services to distribute discounted surplus meals.
44. Encourage bakeries to offer end-of-day discounts on unsold bread.
45. Support local processors that can turn surplus fruit into shelf-stable products.
46. Arrange for suitable food scraps and surplus to become animal feed where permitted.
47. Provide multilingual food-storage guidance tailored to commonly eaten local foods.
48. Test campaign messages with residents to make sure they are clear rather than overwhelming.
49. Publish a city dashboard tracking food-waste prevention and donation progress.
50. Hold an annual challenge inviting neighborhoods to develop and test food-saving ideas.

5. Offer small grants to restaurants that donate safe surplus meals.
6. Train food businesses in safe handling and donation practices.

10. Encourage stores to sell cosmetically imperfect produce at reduced prices.
11. Launch a marketplace where bakeries can sell end-of-day goods at a discount.
12. Help farmers find buyers for produce that does not meet cosmetic standards.
13. Organize volunteer gleaning teams to harvest crops left in fields.
14. Connect local farms with food banks that can accept surplus harvests.
15. Set up a shared commercial kitchen to turn surplus produce into preserved foods.
16. Sponsor workshops on freezing, pickling, and other safe preservation methods.
17. Teach residents how to plan meals around ingredients they already have.
18. Distribute shopping-list templates that help households buy realistic quantities.
19. Offer refrigerator thermometers and guidance on safe food storage.
20. Publish a concise guide explaining the difference between quality and safety date labels.
21. Replace competing food-waste messages with a few clear, consistent instructions.
22. Provide multilingual, picture-based storage guides in libraries and community centers.
23. Invite residents to share recipes for commonly wasted ingredients.
24. Run neighborhood challenges to track and reduce household food waste.
25. Encourage apartment buildings to host supervised food-sharing shelves.
26. Equip schools with supervised share tables for unopened, eligible food.
27. Let students choose portion sizes for selected school meal components.
28. Schedule school lunch periods long enough for students to eat.
29. Audit school cafeteria waste to identify unpopular or oversized meals.
30. Help hospitals forecast meal demand more accurately.
31. Encourage employers to order catered food based on confirmed attendance.
32. Create a rapid pickup service for safe surplus from conferences and events.
33. Ask event organizers to plan donation arrangements before ordering food.
34. Encourage restaurants to offer smaller portions alongside standard portions.
35. Make takeaway containers readily available for restaurant leftovers.
36. Help restaurants track which menu items generate the most waste.
37. Train kitchen staff to use edible trimmings in stocks, sauces, and other dishes.
38. Offer recognition to businesses that report measurable reductions in food waste.
39. Help independent grocers use inventory tools to order closer to demand.
40. Encourage retailers to rotate stock so older products are sold first.
41. Connect wholesalers with secondary buyers for canceled or excess orders.
42. Create a subscription box featuring surplus produce from multiple suppliers.
43. Support mobile markets that bring discounted surplus food to underserved neighborhoods.
44. Coordinate donation pickup schedules so charities can receive food when they are staffed.
45. Fund extra cold-storage space for food pantries.
46. Help community organizations arrange culturally appropriate uses for donated ingredients.
47. Establish a public dashboard showing where edible surplus is being recovered.
48. Provide technical assistance to help food businesses measure waste before choosing interventions.
49. Route unavoidable food scraps to permitted animal-feed programs where regulations allow.
50. Collect inedible food scraps for composting or anaerobic digestion as a last resort.

cells.brief: List 50 distinct ideas for a two-minute short film that can be shot in a single room with two actors. Number them 1 to 50. One sentence each.
cells.text:
1. Two strangers in a waiting room discover they are both waiting to apologize to each other.
2. A burglar hides under a bed while the homeowner practices a confession to an empty room.
3. A chess player realizes every move their opponent makes predicts something about their life.
4. Two siblings divide their late mother’s belongings using increasingly absurd rules.
5. A teacher and student spend detention trying to catch a moth without hurting it.
6. A couple rehearses breaking up, only to disagree about who initiated it.
7. Two astronauts trapped in a cabin debate whether the blinking light means rescue or disaster.
8. A locksmith arrives to open a safe, but its owner keeps changing their mind.
9. Two actors audition for the same role and gradually realize the script describes their meeting.
10. A parent tries to explain a magic trick while their child insists the impossible part was real.
11. Two roommates communicate entirely through notes after an argument about noise.
12. An interviewer discovers the applicant has brought a résumé for the interviewer’s job.
13. A scientist asks an assistant to press a button that will erase one of their memories.
14. Two old friends meet to open a time capsule and find a letter neither remembers writing.
15. A hostage and captor play a word game while waiting for a phone that never rings.
16. A tailor fits a nervous customer for a suit while guessing the occasion incorrectly.
17. Two detectives reconstruct a crime using only objects found on a kitchen table.
18. A person teaches their future self how to make a cup of tea exactly right.
19. A therapist and client quietly swap chairs halfway through a session.
20. Two contestants in a staring contest reveal their entire rivalry without speaking.
21. A chef and food critic argue over a dish neither of them can taste.
22. A houseplant owner interviews a prospective plant-sitter who seems to understand the plant.
23. Two estranged sisters try to record a cheerful birthday message for their father.
24. A librarian catches a patron trying to return a book that has not yet been published.
25. Two strangers wake in a room with one chair and compete to give it away.
26. A magician’s assistant announces that tonight they will reveal a trick the magician does not know.
27. A tenant shows a landlord a mysterious stain that moves whenever neither watches it.
28. Two people assembling a flat-pack shelf use the instructions to negotiate their marriage.
29. A caller and a crisis-line volunteer discover they are sitting on opposite sides of the same room.
30. A painter asks a sitter to hold still while the portrait changes on its own.
31. Two spies exchange code phrases but cannot remember which one is supposed to answer first.
32. A person throws a surprise party for a friend who admits they hate surprises.
33. Two jurors reenact a disagreement using salt and pepper shakers.
34. An inventor demonstrates a machine that translates apologies into what the speaker really means.
35. A dancer coaches an injured rival through the performance they can no longer give.
36. Two people waiting out a storm argue over whether a sealed envelope should be opened.
37. A ghost tries to frighten the only person who can see them into leaving the room.
38. A tailor and customer discover a message stitched inside an old coat.
39. Two siblings race to memorize their childhood home before a buyer arrives.
40. A robot asks its creator why it was programmed to enjoy sad songs.
41. Two neighbors meet through a thin wall and invent a tapping language.
42. A referee and a chess player dispute a match played against an invisible opponent.
43. An archivist and a visitor listen to a recording that seems to describe what they are doing.
44. Two people trapped in an elevator use a deck of cards to decide who should press the alarm.
45. A detective interrogates a suspect who insists they have already had this conversation.
46. A barber gives a customer a haircut while the customer practices asking for a divorce.
47. Two volunteers fold paper cranes for a wish neither wants to say aloud.
48. A sleep researcher tries to keep a subject awake while gradually falling asleep.
49. Two chefs prepare identical sandwiches to settle an old family argument.
50. A person packing to leave finds their roommate has secretly unpacked the same box three times.

cells.brief: List 50 distinct ideas for a two-minute short film that can be shot in a single room with two actors. Number them 1 to 50. One sentence each.
cells.text:
1. Two strangers discover that the key to their locked room is frozen inside an ice cube.
2. A job applicant realizes the interviewer is taking instructions from a goldfish.
3. Siblings dividing an inheritance find a photograph with one of them mysteriously erased.
4. A magician’s assistant reveals the trick before the magician can perform it.
5. Two people on a disastrous first date silently compete to leave the room first.
6. A woman teaching her father to use a phone receives a message meant for him.
7. As a loud machine drowns them out, two negotiators shout themselves into a misunderstanding.
8. A repairer marks broken objects with red stickers, until their partner finds one on their sleeve.
9. Two astronauts practice a farewell message while their spaceship wallpaper peels away.
10. A burglar and a homeowner discover they have both come to steal the same painting.
11. During a power cut, two roommates tell ghost stories that begin to match the shadows around them.
12. A teacher gives a student one last chance to confess, but the teacher is the one who cheated.
13. Two chess players realize the pieces are rearranging themselves whenever they blink.
14. A tailor fitting a wedding suit finds a breakup note hidden in its pocket.
15. A person tries to return a borrowed book without waking its sleeping owner.
16. Two rival chefs must divide the last egg without breaking it.
17. A prisoner and a guard exchange roles for a photograph and struggle to switch back.
18. A grieving woman follows a recipe with her brother, who insists their mother never wrote it down.
19. Two actors rehearsing an argument gradually forget which insults belong to the script.
20. A detective interrogates a suspect whose only answer is to draw increasingly accurate portraits of him.
21. Two neighbors meet through a hole in the wall and disagree about which apartment it belongs to.
22. A scientist asks an assistant to destroy a miniature machine that appears to predict their movements.
23. A couple packing for a trip keeps secretly removing each other’s favorite items from the suitcase.
24. An exhausted parent tries to assemble a toy while their child calmly reads the instructions upside down.
25. A woman attempts to teach her reflection to wave independently, with her skeptical roommate watching.
26. Two musicians tune their instruments until they accidentally play the same forgotten melody.
27. An antique dealer and a customer haggle over a clock that counts backward.
28. Two friends discover that every time they applaud, an object in the room disappears.
29. A therapist and a client switch chairs, and both immediately become more honest.
30. A thief trapped under a bed watches the room’s occupant prepare an elaborate surprise for them.
31. Two office workers race to shred a document before either can read what the other wrote.
32. A person rehearses a marriage proposal with a friend who keeps changing the answer.
33. Two siblings try to identify the owner of a mysterious sound coming from a sealed cardboard box.
34. A customer demands a refund from a fortune teller after the predicted disaster fails to happen.
35. An artist paints a portrait while the sitter subtly alters the pose each time the brush lifts.
36. Two people sorting laundry discover a shirt that fits neither of them but bears both their names.
37. A scientist and a volunteer test a lie detector that rings whenever either tells the truth.
38. A host sets a perfect dinner table while their guest quietly rearranges it according to a map.
39. Two former best friends meet to exchange belongings and find they each kept the same childhood drawing.
40. A contestant practices an acceptance speech as their friend repeatedly interrupts with increasingly ridiculous awards.
41. Two cleaners discover a hidden message beneath layers of paint and argue over whether to expose it.
42. A person offers their roommate a button that promises to erase one embarrassing memory.
43. Two exhausted jurors build a tiny courtroom from stationery to reenact the case.
44. A dancer teaches a partner a routine in which each missed step reveals a hidden note on the floor.
45. An inventor demonstrates an automatic apology machine that keeps apologizing to the wrong person.
46. Two people receive identical letters instructing each to give the other an unnamed object.
47. A caretaker tries to convince a stubborn patient to take medicine by disguising it as a magic trick.
48. Two friends play a game of dares that ends when one is asked to open a long-locked drawer.
49. A seamstress unpicks a damaged coat while its owner tells a different story about every tear.
50. Two strangers sheltering from a storm discover that each has half of the same torn map.

cells.brief: List 50 distinct ideas for a two-minute short film that can be shot in a single room with two actors. Number them 1 to 50. One sentence each.
cells.text:
1. Two strangers discover that a crack in the wall is growing whenever they lie.
2. A cleaner finds a suitcase full of cash, just as the room’s owner returns.
3. A couple divides their belongings with tape until the line reaches their sleeping dog’s empty bed.
4. A magician’s assistant discovers that the disappearing trick has made the magician invisible.
5. Two chess players realize the pieces move themselves whenever they look away.
6. A patient tries to conceal a gift from the nurse treating their broken arm.
7. Two siblings open a time capsule and find a photograph taken that morning.
8. A thief pauses mid-robbery to help the homeowner assemble a flat-pack chair.
9. As construction noise swells, two people shout louder and louder, each misunderstanding the other’s warning.
10. A meticulous repairer labels broken objects for disposal until their partner places a label on their own sleeve.
11. Two job applicants compete for a single chair while waiting for an interview that never begins.
12. A person rehearses a breakup speech to a mannequin, which their partner quietly swaps places with.
13. A chef and a critic communicate entirely through the arrangement of food on a plate.
14. Two astronauts watch a loose screw float across their cabin and scramble to find where it belongs.
15. A landlord paints over a water stain that keeps reappearing in the shape of a face.
16. Two prisoners use shadows on the wall to plan an escape, then discover the shadows can move independently.
17. A tailor notices that every alteration to a customer’s coat changes the customer’s posture and personality.
18. Two people trapped in an elevator compete to remain polite as their urgent needs become obvious.
19. A child teaches a forgetful grandparent a card trick, only to learn the grandparent invented it.
20. A detective interrogates a suspect whose reflections keep contradicting their gestures.
21. Two rival florists must revive the same wilting flower before a timer runs out.
22. A person receives a present from their partner and finds their own missing wedding ring inside.
23. Two dancers improvise around a puddle that inexplicably follows their feet.
24. A librarian and a reader race to catch letters escaping from an old book.
25. A hostage quietly helps their captor practice asking for a raise over the phone.
26. Two artists draw portraits of each other, each secretly making the other look happier.
27. A person tries to hide a surprise party’s single balloon from the guest of honor.
28. Two scientists discover that a houseplant responds only to insults, then struggle to hurt its feelings.
29. A pair of twins swap clothes to fool a security camera, forgetting they are the only people in the room.
30. Two people play rock-paper-scissors to decide who will open a mysterious box, then both refuse to win.
31. A pianist discovers that each wrong note rearranges the furniture.
32. A babysitter tries to put a wide-awake child to bed while pretending to be asleep.
33. Two exes encounter each other while packing the last box in their shared apartment.
34. A watchmaker and a customer relive the same minute whenever a repaired clock strikes.
35. Two strangers sit on opposite sides of a room, passing an increasingly elaborate paper airplane between them.
36. A detective discovers that the supposedly dead body is trying not to sneeze.
37. A person teaching their partner sign language accidentally learns what their partner has been hiding.
38. Two bakers try to disguise a collapsed cake before the customer returns.
39. A photographer asks a reluctant subject to smile, then slowly reveals why the picture matters.
40. Two people discover a locked door painted on the wall and work out how to open it.
41. A gambler bets their last coin against a silent opponent who turns out to be their future self.
42. A teacher confiscates a student’s doodle and finds a drawing of the teacher’s secret ambition.
43. Two roommates argue over a thermostat until frost begins creeping across the room.
44. A person tries to apologize with flowers, but their recipient keeps rearranging them into unmistakably rude shapes.
45. Two museum guards notice that a portrait’s eyes follow only one of them.
46. A tailor and customer silently negotiate how much of a torn wedding dress can be saved.
47. Two enemies shelter from a storm and discover they are knitting the same unfinished scarf.
48. A person follows a trail of sticky notes around the room to find their partner’s hidden proposal.
49. Two card players realize that every card they discard vanishes from the world outside the game.
50. A janitor and an executive trade jackets as a joke, then struggle to get the other to trade back.

cells.brief: List 50 distinct ideas for reducing food waste in a mid-size city. Number them 1 to 50. One sentence each.
cells.text:
1. Offer households free food-waste audits to identify their biggest sources of waste.
2. Run a public campaign on planning meals before shopping.
3. Distribute reusable shopping lists organized by store section.
4. Teach residents how to interpret “best before” and expiration dates.
5. Offer workshops on storing produce to extend its freshness.
6. Create a citywide directory of places that accept surplus food.
7. Fund neighborhood community fridges with regular safety inspections.
8. Coordinate volunteers to transport surplus meals from businesses to shelters.
9. Give restaurants grants to buy equipment for safely storing surplus food.
10. Connect grocery stores with food banks through a real-time donation platform.
11. Help schools donate unopened surplus meals where regulations permit.
12. Encourage cafeterias to use smaller serving utensils and offer second helpings.
13. Let students preorder school lunches so kitchens can prepare accurate quantities.
14. Train school cafeteria staff to track and reduce kitchen waste.
15. Add share tables in schools for unopened, unwanted food.
16. Offer restaurants tools to forecast demand using past sales data.
17. Encourage restaurants to offer smaller portion options.
18. Provide reusable containers for customers to take leftovers home.
19. Promote discounted end-of-day sales of unsold prepared food.
20. Create a city-backed marketplace for imperfect produce.
21. Help farmers sell surplus crops through pop-up neighborhood markets.
22. Organize volunteer gleaning teams to harvest crops that would otherwise be left in fields.
23. Connect local farmers with processors who can turn surplus produce into shelf-stable products.
24. Support commercial kitchens that make soups and sauces from donated surplus ingredients.
25. Encourage grocery stores to sell individual fruits and vegetables rather than only large packs.
26. Ask retailers to place soon-to-expire items in clearly marked discount sections.
27. Provide small businesses with guidance on safe food donation.
28. Recognize businesses that meet measurable food-waste reduction goals.
29. Include food-waste prevention requirements in city catering contracts.
30. Require large municipal events to develop surplus-food donation plans.
31. Help event organizers estimate attendance and adjust catering orders.
32. Offer cooking classes focused on using leftovers creatively.
33. Publish seasonal recipes that use commonly wasted ingredients.
34. Teach residents how to freeze food safely in convenient portions.
35. Create a neighborhood exchange for homegrown produce.
36. Partner with apartment managers to share food-storage tips with tenants.
37. Work with employers to reduce overordering for meetings and office events.
38. Encourage hotels to replace oversized buffets with smaller batches replenished as needed.
39. Help hospitals tailor meal orders to patients’ preferences and schedules.
40. Support care homes in adjusting menus based on residents’ feedback and plate waste.
41. Introduce pay-as-you-feel community meals made with safe surplus ingredients.
42. Train food pantry staff to manage inventory using a first-in, first-out system.
43. Provide food pantries with refrigeration to accept more perishable donations.
44. Coordinate donation pickup schedules so charities receive food they can distribute promptly.
45. Create a municipal dashboard tracking food waste and recovery over time.
46. Provide grants for businesses to measure food waste by source.
47. Convene retailers, charities, farmers, and residents to coordinate local prevention efforts.
48. Pilot neighborhood drop-off points for surplus shelf-stable food.
49. Provide compost collection for unavoidable food scraps after edible food has been prioritized for people.
50. Arrange for suitable food scraps to become animal feed where local rules allow.

cells.brief: List 50 distinct ideas for reducing food waste in a mid-size city. Number them 1 to 50. One sentence each.
cells.text:
1. Create a citywide food-rescue hotline that connects businesses with nearby charities.
2. Build a shared map of organizations that accept surplus food.
3. Fund refrigerated vans to collect donations from grocery stores.
4. Install community fridges in accessible, regularly monitored locations.
5. Offer small grants to restaurants that donate safe surplus meals.
6. Train food businesses in safe handling and donation practices.
7. Establish clear labeling standards for donated food and its storage requirements.
8. Introduce a simple “use soon” tag for safe food nearing its expiration date.
9. Create dedicated discount shelves for short-dated groceries.
10. Encourage stores to sell cosmetically imperfect produce at reduced prices.
11. Launch a marketplace where bakeries can sell end-of-day goods at a discount.
12. Help farmers find buyers for produce that does not meet cosmetic standards.
13. Organize volunteer gleaning teams to harvest crops left in fields.
14. Connect local farms with food banks that can accept surplus harvests.
15. Set up a shared commercial kitchen to turn surplus produce into preserved foods.
16. Sponsor workshops on freezing, pickling, and other safe preservation methods.
17. Teach residents how to plan meals around ingredients they already have.
18. Distribute shopping-list templates that help households buy realistic quantities.
19. Offer refrigerator thermometers and guidance on safe food storage.
20. Publish a concise guide explaining the difference between quality and safety date labels.
21. Replace competing food-waste messages with a few clear, consistent instructions.
22. Provide multilingual, picture-based storage guides in libraries and community centers.
23. Invite residents to share recipes for commonly wasted ingredients.
24. Run neighborhood challenges to track and reduce household food waste.
25. Encourage apartment buildings to host supervised food-sharing shelves.
26. Equip schools with supervised share tables for unopened, eligible food.
27. Let students choose portion sizes for selected school meal components.
28. Schedule school lunch periods long enough for students to eat.
29. Audit school cafeteria waste to identify unpopular or oversized meals.
30. Help hospitals forecast meal demand more accurately.
31. Encourage employers to order catered food based on confirmed attendance.
32. Create a rapid pickup service for safe surplus from conferences and events.
33. Ask event organizers to plan donation arrangements before ordering food.
34. Encourage restaurants to offer smaller portions alongside standard portions.
35. Make takeaway containers readily available for restaurant leftovers.
36. Help restaurants track which menu items generate the most waste.
37. Train kitchen staff to use edible trimmings in stocks, sauces, and other dishes.
38. Offer recognition to businesses that report measurable reductions in food waste.
39. Help independent grocers use inventory tools to order closer to demand.
40. Encourage retailers to rotate stock so older products are sold first.
41. Connect wholesalers with secondary buyers for canceled or excess orders.
42. Create a subscription box featuring surplus produce from multiple suppliers.
43. Support mobile markets that bring discounted surplus food to underserved neighborhoods.
44. Coordinate donation pickup schedules so charities can receive food when they are staffed.
45. Fund extra cold-storage space for food pantries.
46. Help community organizations arrange culturally appropriate uses for donated ingredients.
47. Establish a public dashboard showing where edible surplus is being recovered.
48. Provide technical assistance to help food businesses measure waste before choosing interventions.
49. Route unavoidable food scraps to permitted animal-feed programs where regulations allow.
50. Collect inedible food scraps for composting or anaerobic digestion as a last resort.

cells.brief: List 50 distinct ideas for a two-minute short film that can be shot in a single room with two actors. Number them 1 to 50. One sentence each.
cells.text:
1. Two strangers in a waiting room discover they are both waiting to apologize to each other.
2. A burglar hides under a bed while the homeowner practices a confession to an empty room.
3. A chess player realizes every move their opponent makes predicts something about their life.
4. Two siblings divide their late mother’s belongings using increasingly absurd rules.
5. A teacher and student spend detention trying to catch a moth without hurting it.
6. A couple rehearses breaking up, only to disagree about who initiated it.
7. Two astronauts trapped in a cabin debate whether the blinking light means rescue or disaster.
8. A locksmith arrives to open a safe, but its owner keeps changing their mind.
9. Two actors audition for the same role and gradually realize the script describes their meeting.
10. A parent tries to explain a magic trick while their child insists the impossible part was real.
11. Two roommates communicate entirely through notes after an argument about noise.
12. An interviewer discovers the applicant has brought a résumé for the interviewer’s job.
13. A scientist asks an assistant to press a button that will erase one of their memories.
14. Two old friends meet to open a time capsule and find a letter neither remembers writing.
15. A hostage and captor play a word game while waiting for a phone that never rings.
16. A tailor fits a nervous customer for a suit while guessing the occasion incorrectly.
17. Two detectives reconstruct a crime using only objects found on a kitchen table.
18. A person teaches their future self how to make a cup of tea exactly right.
19. A therapist and client quietly swap chairs halfway through a session.
20. Two contestants in a staring contest reveal their entire rivalry without speaking.
21. A chef and food critic argue over a dish neither of them can taste.
22. A houseplant owner interviews a prospective plant-sitter who seems to understand the plant.
23. Two estranged sisters try to record a cheerful birthday message for their father.
24. A librarian catches a patron trying to return a book that has not yet been published.
25. Two strangers wake in a room with one chair and compete to give it away.
26. A magician’s assistant announces that tonight they will reveal a trick the magician does not know.
27. A tenant shows a landlord a mysterious stain that moves whenever neither watches it.
28. Two people assembling a flat-pack shelf use the instructions to negotiate their marriage.
29. A caller and a crisis-line volunteer discover they are sitting on opposite sides of the same room.
30. A painter asks a sitter to hold still while the portrait changes on its own.
31. Two spies exchange code phrases but cannot remember which one is supposed to answer first.
32. A person throws a surprise party for a friend who admits they hate surprises.
33. Two jurors reenact a disagreement using salt and pepper shakers.
34. An inventor demonstrates a machine that translates apologies into what the speaker really means.
35. A dancer coaches an injured rival through the performance they can no longer give.
36. Two people waiting out a storm argue over whether a sealed envelope should be opened.
37. A ghost tries to frighten the only person who can see them into leaving the room.
38. A tailor and customer discover a message stitched inside an old coat.
39. Two siblings race to memorize their childhood home before a buyer arrives.
40. A robot asks its creator why it was programmed to enjoy sad songs.
41. Two neighbors meet through a thin wall and invent a tapping language.
42. A referee and a chess player dispute a match played against an invisible opponent.
43. An archivist and a visitor listen to a recording that seems to describe what they are doing.
44. Two people trapped in an elevator use a deck of cards to decide who should press the alarm.
45. A detective interrogates a suspect who insists they have already had this conversation.
46. A barber gives a customer a haircut while the customer practices asking for a divorce.
47. Two volunteers fold paper cranes for a wish neither wants to say aloud.
48. A sleep researcher tries to keep a subject awake while gradually falling asleep.
49. Two chefs prepare identical sandwiches to settle an old family argument.
50. A person packing to leave finds their roommate has secretly unpacked the same box three times.

cells.brief: List 50 distinct ideas for a two-minute short film that can be shot in a single room with two actors. Number them 1 to 50. One sentence each.
cells.text:
1. A locksmith opens a stranger’s suitcase and finds a key labeled with the exact time of his death, two minutes from now.
2. Two siblings divide their late mother’s belongings by flipping a coin that keeps landing on its edge.
3. A job applicant realizes the interviewer is asking questions from a conversation they will have tomorrow.
4. Two burglars hiding in a closet discover they were hired to steal from each other.
5. A woman teaches her father how to use a video call, though both know there is nobody left to call.
6. A hostage negotiator discovers the person she’s negotiating with is also tied to a chair.
7. Two strangers in a waiting room compete to prove they deserve the last seat in heaven.
8. A chef and a food critic taste an invisible dish that brings back sharply different memories.
9. A detective interrogates a suspect whose shadow keeps confessing.
10. Two astronauts rehearse the speech they’ll give if they make it home, then quietly edit out each other.
11. A tenant argues with her landlord over a mirror that shows the room exactly one minute into the future.
12. Two rival magicians try to steal each other’s secrets while handcuffed together.
13. A woman receives a birthday cake from her future self, who refuses to explain the single unlit candle.
14. Two employees practice firing each other because neither knows which one is the boss.
15. A chess player bargains with Death for one more move, only to discover Death doesn’t know the rules.
16. A couple packs an apartment while inventing increasingly absurd explanations for why they’re separating.
17. An inventor demonstrates a machine that translates silence, and her skeptical guest stops speaking.
18. Two actors audition for the same role, then realize the script describes the audition itself.
19. A museum guard catches a thief trying to return a painting before anyone notices it was stolen.
20. Two scientists watch an egg hatch something only one of them can see.
21. A man asks a stranger to help him remember a password, revealing more about his life with every guess.
22. Two etiquette experts remain impeccably polite while competing for the only working phone charger.
23. A tattoo artist is asked to cover a name that keeps reappearing under the fresh ink.
24. Two people meet to exchange identical briefcases, but each insists theirs is the empty one.
25. A grandmother and grandson build a blanket fort to shelter from an argument neither wants to start.
26. A therapist and patient switch chairs, and the patient turns out to be alarmingly good at the job.
27. Two time travelers arrive in the same room to prevent each other from moving a chair.
28. A wedding officiant helps a bride practice her vows, gradually realizing they’re addressed to him.
29. Two prisoners discover their cell door is unlocked and must decide who will be brave enough to leave first.
30. A ventriloquist’s dummy is missing, so her assistant reluctantly agrees to fill in for an audition.
31. A witness describes a crime while the sketch artist draws a portrait that looks increasingly like herself.
32. Two neighbors attempt a silent argument through handwritten notes because a baby is sleeping in the next room.
33. A tailor measures a customer for a suit intended to make him disappear in a crowd.
34. Two gods sit at a kitchen table arguing over who accidentally invented mosquitoes.
35. A woman hires an impersonator to play her at a difficult family dinner, then finds herself auditioning for the role.
36. Two collectors bid against each other for a sealed envelope that supposedly contains the meaning of life.
37. A pianist with stage fright plays for an audience of one, who insists on being the piano.
38. A man wakes from surgery to find his surgeon stitching up a banana and refusing to explain.
39. Two exes meet to exchange houseplants and discover each has been caring for the other’s favorite badly on purpose.
40. A customs officer inspects a traveler’s bag and finds it contains only objects the officer has lost.
41. Two meteorologists report increasingly intimate emotional forecasts using magnets on a refrigerator.
42. A handwriting expert examines a ransom note and recognizes a message she wrote to herself as a child.
43. Two roommates perform an elaborate funeral for a housefly, each using the eulogy to air grievances.
44. A translator struggles to convey a love confession because the speaker keeps changing their mind mid-sentence.
45. Two people play hide-and-seek in a bare room, and one of them somehow vanishes.
46. A fortune-teller refuses payment from a client whose palm shows a future ending in the next two minutes.
47. Two rival bakers judge a cake neither of them made, each afraid to admit it’s better than theirs.
48. A robot asks its maker to remove one painful memory, then reveals the memory is of her.
49. Two strangers find themselves wearing each other’s clothes after waking up in a locked hotel room.
50. A sound engineer records a door creak for a horror film while her assistant gradually makes it sound like a love song.

9. A magician’s assistant refuses to reveal how a trick went wrong unless the magician apologizes.
10. Two rival chefs must make dinner from a single can of beans and whatever they can find in a kitchen.
11. A person meets their future self, who has returned solely to borrow a pen.
12. Two friends recording a podcast discover that the microphone picks up thoughts they are too polite to say.
13. A landlord and tenant inspect a suspicious stain that moves whenever neither is looking.
14. An art forger and a collector negotiate over a painting that both know is fake.
15. Two actors audition for the same role and gradually begin performing each other’s lives.
16. A wedding planner tries to convince a bride to leave the bathroom before the ceremony, but the planner is hiding a confession.
17. A night-shift cleaner finds a talking vending machine and demands a refund for every snack it has ever stolen.
18. Two estranged friends attempt to assemble a flat-pack bookshelf without mentioning why they stopped speaking.
19. A student accuses a professor of stealing their idea, only to discover the professor has the same accusation.

cells.brief: List 50 distinct ideas for a two-minute short film that can be shot in a single room with two actors. Number them 1 to 50. One sentence each.
cells.text:
1. Two strangers discover that a crack in the wall is growing whenever they lie.
2. A cleaner finds a suitcase full of cash, just as the room’s owner returns.
3. A couple divides their belongings with tape until the line reaches their sleeping dog’s empty bed.
4. A magician’s assistant discovers that the disappearing trick has made the magician invisible.
5. Two chess players realize the pieces move themselves whenever they look away.
6. A patient tries to conceal a gift from the nurse treating their broken arm.
7. Two siblings open a time capsule and find a photograph taken that morning.
8. A thief pauses mid-robbery to help the homeowner assemble a flat-pack chair.
9. As construction noise swells, two people shout louder and louder, each misunderstanding the other’s warning.
10. A meticulous repairer labels broken objects for disposal until their partner places a label on their own sleeve.
11. Two job applicants compete for a single chair while waiting for an interview that never begins.
12. A person rehearses a breakup speech to a mannequin, which their partner quietly swaps places with.
13. A chef and a critic communicate entirely through the arrangement of food on a plate.
14. Two astronauts watch a loose screw float across their cabin and scramble to find where it belongs.
15. A landlord paints over a water stain that keeps reappearing in the shape of a face.
16. Two prisoners use shadows on the wall to plan an escape, then discover the shadows can move independently.
17. A tailor notices that every alteration to a customer’s coat changes the customer’s posture and personality.
18. Two people trapped in an elevator compete to remain polite as their urgent needs become obvious.
19. A child teaches a forgetful grandparent a card trick, only to learn the grandparent invented it.
20. A detective interrogates a suspect whose reflections keep contradicting their gestures.
21. Two rival florists must revive the same wilting flower before a timer runs out.
22. A person receives a present from their partner and finds their own missing wedding ring inside.
23. Two dancers improvise around a puddle that inexplicably follows their feet.
24. A librarian and a reader race to catch letters escaping from an old book.
25. A hostage quietly helps their captor practice asking for a raise over the phone.
26. Two artists draw portraits of each other, each secretly making the other look happier.
27. A person tries to hide a surprise party’s single balloon from the guest of honor.
28. Two scientists discover that a houseplant responds only to insults, then struggle to hurt its feelings.
29. A pair of twins swap clothes to fool a security camera, forgetting they are the only people in the room.
30. Two people play rock-paper-scissors to decide who will open a mysterious box, then both refuse to win.
31. A pianist discovers that each wrong note rearranges the furniture.
32. A babysitter tries to put a wide-awake child to bed while pretending to be asleep.
33. Two exes encounter each other while packing the last box in their shared apartment.
34. A watchmaker and a customer relive the same minute whenever a repaired clock strikes.
35. Two strangers sit on opposite sides of a room, passing an increasingly elaborate paper airplane between them.
36. A detective discovers that the supposedly dead body is trying not to sneeze.
37. A person teaching their partner sign language accidentally learns what their partner has been hiding.
38. Two bakers try to disguise a collapsed cake before the customer returns.
39. A photographer asks a reluctant subject to smile, then slowly reveals why the picture matters.
40. Two people discover a locked door painted on the wall and work out how to open it.
41. A gambler bets their last coin against a silent opponent who turns out to be their future self.
42. A teacher confiscates a student’s doodle and finds a drawing of the teacher’s secret ambition.
43. Two roommates argue over a thermostat until frost begins creeping across the room.
44. A person tries to apologize with flowers, but their recipient keeps rearranging them into unmistakably rude shapes.
45. Two museum guards notice that a portrait’s eyes follow only one of them.
46. A tailor and customer silently negotiate how much of a torn wedding dress can be saved.
47. Two enemies shelter from a storm and discover they are knitting the same unfinished scarf.
48. A person follows a trail of sticky notes around the room to find their partner’s hidden proposal.
49. Two card players realize that every card they discard vanishes from the world outside the game.
50. A janitor and an executive trade jackets as a joke, then struggle to get the other to trade back.
